_readme: Queue written by the daily-reel-render task, drained by tools/apply_additions.py during tools/sync.bat. The task must NOT edit calendar.md or review-state.json directly - it queues here instead, and sync.bat folds these in AFTER pulling, on top of whatever the desk decided today. That is what stops the two files conflicting. Adds only: an existing calendar row (keyed on date + post title) is left exactly as the desk left it, and so is an existing review-state key - with one exception, the render flip (content: awaiting-render or rerender -> in-review, plus new revisions entries), which is what tells the desk a cut now exists. It can never write an approval; see the module docstring in tools/apply_additions.py.

revisions.changed: Fixed the citation collision behind "The WFDF reference is blocking the content". The "WFDF Rules of Ultimate 2025-2028" line sits at a fixed y (1150); on scene 2 the body wrapped to six lines at 36px, putting its last baseline at 1140 and overlapping the citation's ink by 17px. Everything was inside the margins, so v1's layout check reported clean. render_v3.py gained fit_body(), the body-paragraph twin of fit_kicker(): largest integer size up to 36px whose wrapped block clears the citation, line height scaled with it, floor 80% (29px), SystemExit below that. Scene 2 now renders at 31px over five lines, scene 4 at 35px, scene 6 unchanged at 36px. No word of the approved script changed. Nine scenes, exact CFR via encode.py, 29.50s, longest sustained dull-orange run 0.20s. v1 archived as reel18-straddle-and-wrapping.v1.mp4.

Scene 4's body renders at 29px, the 80% floor of fit_body(), because its four-line headline leaves nothing larger clearing the citation.
